paragraphs: Decision center: the work of diesel service technicians and mechanics is to turn a vehicle's symptoms into a reviewable chain of handling — first asking questions and reading fault codes and instrument values, then confirming the cause of the fault against the manufacturer's service manual and measured values, then disassembling and inspecting, replacing or repairing, reassembling to specification and rechecking, and finally road testing to verify and leaving the process as a work order and records. The focus of judgment is not whether you look like a mechanic, but whether every step along the chain of questioning and initial inspection — measurement and diagnosis — disassembly and repair — reassembly and verification — recording and delivery has a basis and is traceable, so that both colleagues and customers can review it.

Worth trying first: you are willing to troubleshoot step by step according to the manual and safety procedures rather than taking things apart first and thinking later, can stay patient and careful amid oil, noise and confined spaces, can accept the protective requirements of lifting, electrical, welding and high-pressure fuel system work, can record measured values and replaced parts truthfully, and would rather check safety components (brakes, steering, wheel bearings) one extra time.

Requires caution: if you are impatient about looking things up and keeping records, tend to replace parts by feel, or are unwilling to wear protective equipment and find torque and clearance rechecks troublesome, or expect to do only electrical and computer diagnosis and never touch the dirty or heavy work, then the actual workshop experience usually does not match expectations.

Low-risk verification: use a fictional vehicle fault description and three sets of measurement data (such as fuel pressure, cylinder pressure and brake lining thickness) to complete an exercise in listing the information that needs verification, writing out the troubleshooting order according to the manual, giving conclusions and the components to be replaced or rechecked, and writing a work order record; this only verifies whether you are willing to check item by item against the manual and data and to document it. The exercise uses fictional material, does not dismantle any real vehicle and does not carry out any real lifting, electrical, welding or fuel system work, and does not equal completed training, repair authorization or industry certification.

Decision center: whether the symptoms described by the customer, the fault codes and the measurement data can be organised into a chain of handling and delivery that colleagues can understand, that can be reproduced after reassembly, and that can be written into a work order.

The work is mainly workshop based, with occasional roadside and route work: exposure to contaminants (dust, gases, odours and so on) 85% every day, exposure to distracting or uncomfortable noise 81% every day, using hands to handle, control or feel objects and tools 80% continuously or almost continuously, wearing common protective or safety equipment 78% every day, indoors but without environmental control 74% every day, being in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 68% every day; face-to-face discussion with individuals and teams 90% every day; the importance of precision or accuracy is considered extremely important by 53%, very high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers 72%, a typical workweek longer than 40 hours 53%, time pressure 40% every day.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 49-3031.00 (titled Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists by O*NET and Diesel Service Technicians and Mechanics by the BLS Occupational Outlook), whose core is the inspection, diagnosis, repair and overhaul of vehicles powered by diesel engines and of diesel engines; adjacent positions have different duties — automotive service technicians and mechanics focus mainly on petrol-engined passenger cars and light vehicles, automotive body and glass repairers handle body structure and glass installation, heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers focus on transport tasks, and industrial machinery mechanics maintain factory production equipment. The specific scope is governed by the job, the manufacturer's technical information and the authorization, and is not inferred from the job title.

Inputs that must be verified: the fault symptoms and operating conditions described by the customer or dispatcher, fault codes and instrument readings, the manufacturer's service technical information and labour time allowances, the specifications, torques and clearances of safety components, whether parts are genuine and traceable, and the safety procedures for lifting and for electrical, welding and high-pressure fuel system work. What must not be done: do not replace assemblies by feel, do not dismantle safety components before the cause of the fault is confirmed, do not use counterfeit or substandard parts, do not temporarily replace emission control devices or disable the onboard emission diagnostic system to get a vehicle through an emission inspection, do not omit torque and clearance rechecks and road test verification, and do not write records of measured values and replaced parts that differ from reality.

Fit judgments should be made in combination with whether troubleshooting can be done item by item against the manual and measured values, tolerance for working amid oil, noise and confined spaces, the importance attached to rechecking safety components and torque and clearances, and whether documentation is still kept under time pressure, and should not be replaced by a self-assessment of having good hands or working fast; these all need to be confirmed in supervised actual work and training.

All paper exercises on this page use fictional material; real lifting, dismantling and assembly, electrical and welding work, high-pressure fuel system and emission-related repairs must be carried out by personnel with the corresponding capability and authorization, in compliance with safety procedures and the manufacturer's technical requirements and with local rules on repair operations and work practices. Individuals must not carry out such work without protection or authorization, and this page does not constitute safety, compliance or legal advice.

The object of this occupation's work is the technical condition of vehicles and diesel-powered equipment: the fault symptoms described by the customer, fault codes and instrument readings, oil and wear traces, disassembly findings and gauge readings, and the cause of the fault confirmed by measured values; the outputs are work orders and repair records, test data and replaced parts lists, road test and delivery confirmation, and waste oil and solid waste disposal records; the basis for judgment is the manufacturer's service technical information and labour time allowances, safety operating procedures and quality control requirements, not personal experience or job title.

Judgment one: whether the fault symptoms have been reconstructed — whether the operating conditions and the time of occurrence are clarified first, and whether fault codes are read and current instrument values recorded, rather than directly accepting a claim that something is probably broken.

Judgment two: whether the diagnosis is based on measured values — whether instruments, listening and road testing are used to rule things out item by item in the order given by the manual, and whether measured data such as pressure, temperature, clearance or voltage are recorded, rather than concluding from sound and experience alone.

Judgment three: whether safety components are correctly rechecked — whether components directly related to driving safety, such as brakes, steering and wheel bearings, are replaced to specification, reassembled to the specified torque and clearance, and confirmed by recheck and road test.

Judgment four: whether the work keeps to safety and compliance boundaries — whether lifting and support, electrical isolation, welding protection, high-pressure fuel system depressurisation and emission-related repairs are carried out according to procedure, whether genuine and traceable parts are used, and whether waste oil and solid waste disposal records are kept.

Judgment five: whether the records and delivery can be reviewed — whether the work order clearly states the cause of the fault, the handling method, replaced parts and measured values, and whether items still requiring recheck or observation are noted, so that colleagues, customers and quality inspectors can verify on that basis.

Judgment six: whether collaboration and escalation are timely — when facing assembly overhauls, complex electrical diagnosis, structural modification or emission-related determinations that exceed one's capability or authorization, whether guidance is sought according to the process or the matter is passed to personnel with the right conditions, rather than forcing it through.

Environment and pace: mainly workshop work, with occasional repairs at the roadside or at a work site; workshop ventilation is relatively good but it is sometimes noisy; exposure to contaminants 85% every day, noise 81% every day, indoors but without environmental control 74% every day, being in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 68% every day; using hands to handle and control tools 80% continuously or almost continuously, wearing common protective or safety equipment 78% every day; face-to-face discussion with individuals and teams 90% every day; a typical workweek longer than 40 hours 53%, time pressure 40% every day.

The work of diesel service technicians and mechanics can be divided into three linked but independent work areas. The first is questioning and diagnosis: confirming the real fault symptoms and operating conditions with the customer or dispatcher, determining the cause of the fault with test instruments, diagnostic tools, listening and road testing, reading fault codes and measuring parameters such as pressure, temperature, clearance and voltage, deciding whether adjustment, replacement or an assembly overhaul is needed, and confirming the condition of safety components. The second is dismantling and overhaul: lifting vehicles and heavy components with jacks and lifting gear, dismantling and overhauling internal combustion engines, pumps, generators, transmissions, clutches and differentials, repairing or replacing pistons, bearings, gears and valves, servicing and adjusting fuel injection systems, emission control devices, brakes, steering and suspension, and reassembling to specification and rechecking torques and clearances. The third is maintenance and delivery: carrying out routine servicing such as oil changes and battery and lubrication checks, taking exhaust and emission-related measurements and adjustments, disposing of waste oil and reducing solid waste as required by environmental rules, recording work orders and replaced parts, and performing road test and delivery confirmation. The three work areas proceed according to safety procedures and the manufacturer's technical information, and the pace is determined by the workshop schedule and the customer's need for the vehicle.

The comparison must verify item by item against job duties, the manufacturer's technical information and work authorization, and cannot be exchanged by job title.
Core purpose

Restore vehicles and equipment powered by diesel engines to a technical condition in which they can operate safely and reliably, and leave the cause of the fault, the handling method and replaced parts as a verifiable record.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: automotive service technicians and mechanics restore the technical condition of petrol passenger cars and light vehicles; body and glass repairers restore body structure and glass installation; heavy truck drivers complete transport tasks and ensure safety en route; industrial machinery mechanics keep factory equipment available.
Main objects and basis

The objects are diesel engines, assemblies such as transmission, brakes, steering and suspension, fuel injection and emission control and electrical and hydraulic components, and fault codes and measured values and service manuals; the basis is the manufacturer's service technical information and labour time allowances, safety operating procedures and quality control requirements.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: petrol vehicle assemblies and onboard electronic controls (automotive repair specifications); body structure and glass (panel beating and installation specifications); transport tasks and daily vehicle checks (road transport and safety rules); factory equipment and production lines (equipment maintenance procedures).
Core process

Questioning and initial inspection → code reading and measurement → locating by listening and road test → dismantling and determination → replacement or repair → reassembly and torque and clearance recheck → road test verification → recording and delivery.

Processes of adjacent positions: petrol vehicle diagnosis and repair (automotive service technicians); panel straightening and glass installation (body and glass staff); pre-trip inspection and transport execution (heavy truck drivers); preventive maintenance and equipment breakdown repair (industrial machinery mechanics).
Main outputs

Work orders and repair records, fault codes and measurement data, dismantling and replaced parts lists, reassembly and torque and clearance recheck records, road test and delivery confirmation, and waste oil and solid waste disposal records.
Outputs of adjacent positions: petrol vehicle repair records; body and glass repair results; transport task and driving records; equipment maintenance and repair records.
Responsible parties

People in this occupation are responsible for repair quality, the correct reassembly of safety components and the truthfulness and completeness of records; lifting, electrical, welding and high-pressure fuel system work must follow safety procedures, and emission-related repairs must not be used to get a vehicle through inspection by temporarily replacing emission control devices or disabling the onboard emission diagnostic system.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: automotive service technicians are responsible for petrol vehicle repair quality; body and glass staff are responsible for structure and installation; heavy truck drivers are responsible for transport safety and on-route handling; industrial machinery mechanics are responsible for the operating condition of equipment.
Collaboration and supervision

Confirm the fault and costs with the service adviser or customer, check the source and traceability information of parts with the parts supply, and hand over inspection conclusions to the technical lead and quality inspectors; assembly overhauls, complex electrical diagnosis and structural modification must follow the escalation process or be passed to personnel with the right conditions.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: automotive service technicians with service reception and the parts department; body and glass staff with claims assessment and insurance; heavy truck drivers with dispatch and repair stations; industrial machinery mechanics with production and equipment management.

Motor vehicle repair operators in China file with the county-level transport authority of their location after registration, filing is free of charge, and the scope and category follow the business items. Article 12 requires at least 1 person each for the technical lead, quality inspection and reception and for each type of repair personnel in categories one and two; category three comprehensive minor repairs, engine, body, electrical and automatic transmission repair also require a technical lead and quality inspection, and this cannot be omitted. Quality inspection personnel must hold a compatible driving licence, so the driving threshold is not uniform for all repair workers; enterprise filing does not replace individual skills or position authority. Diesel service technicians and mechanics (United States O*NET-SOC 49-3031.00; titled Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists by O*NET and Diesel Service Technicians and Mechanics by the BLS Occupational Outlook): inspect, diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul buses, trucks and other vehicles powered by diesel engines, and maintain and repair various diesel engines, including mechanics who mainly work on automotive or marine diesel engines. Typical work includes using hand tools (screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, pressure gauges and precision instruments) and power tools (pneumatic wrenches, lathes, welding equipment, jacks and lifting gear), checking safety components such as the brake system, steering mechanism and wheel bearings, lifting vehicles and heavy components with hydraulic jacks or lifting gear, adjusting and replacing brake linings, aligning wheels and reassembling at the specified torque, connecting test instruments to equipment to read gauges and meters in order to diagnose faults, reading codes with diagnostic tools and confirming by listening and road testing, dismantling and overhauling internal combustion engines, pumps, generators, transmissions, clutches and differentials, repairing or replacing pistons, bearings, gears and valves, servicing fuel injection systems and emission control devices, carrying out routine servicing such as oil changes, battery checks and lubrication, and disposing of waste oil and reducing solid waste as required by environmental rules. The work routinely involves oil, dust, noise and confined spaces, and protective equipment must be used according to safety procedures.

This table compares diesel service technicians and mechanics with six adjacent positions row by row across core work and outputs, key differences, and basis for choice. The principle for choosing adjacent positions is that they are easily confused on a real work site, or have a job rotation or transfer relationship with this occupation. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them but to explain their respective duty boundaries and scopes of authorization, and to avoid exchanging them by job title.

The comparison should rest on three things: first, the work object (vehicles powered by diesel engines and various diesel engines, or petrol passenger cars, body structure, transport tasks or factory equipment); second, the basis and authorization (the respective application of the manufacturer's service technical information and safety operating procedures, road transport rules, and equipment maintenance procedures); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for repair quality and the reassembly of safety components, and who is responsible for transport safety or equipment operation). Where the three are inconsistent, the actual duties of the position and the authorisation documents of the institution concerned should prevail.

The basis for choice can follow three clues: if the interest is in fault diagnosis and overhaul of diesel engines, transmissions and hydraulic systems, this occupation is the closest; if you would rather deal with standardized quick service on passenger cars and onboard electronic controls, automotive service technicians and mechanics are more suitable; if you prefer equipment structure and installation precision, millwrights and industrial machinery mechanics are closer; if you want to take on transport and on-route handling responsibility on the operating side, heavy truck driver is another path. What needs to be built up when transferring is knowledge of the objects, safety procedures and the scope of authorization, not just tool proficiency.

Boundaries and sources: the differences listed in this table are based on the O*NET occupational profiles and work context data, the BLS Occupational Outlook descriptions of positions and preparation levels, and the scope of application of the mainland China Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair and the national occupational skill standard for automotive repairers. The qualification and authorization requirements of adjacent positions cannot substitute for one another; this page does not infer income levels or hiring conditions from job titles.
Automotive service technicians and mechanics

Servicing petrol-engined passenger cars and light vehicles: diagnosing engine and onboard electronic control faults, servicing brake, steering, suspension, air conditioning and electrical systems, carrying out oil changes and maintenance, and completing quick service and routine repairs to standard labour times.

The objects and assemblies differ: this occupation focuses on diesel engines and the assemblies and hydraulic and pneumatic circuits of heavy vehicles such as buses and trucks, with assembly overhauls and high-pressure fuel system work being common; automotive service technicians deal more with passenger car electronic controls and standardized servicing, with a lower share of body and chassis work. Both require code reading and measurement, but the manual systems, tools and safety requirements differ.

If you want a relatively gentler entry threshold and a more standardized working environment and vehicle types, you can start in the automotive service technician direction; if you are willing to build up in the diesel and heavy vehicle direction, the technical depth of this occupation is more pronounced. When transferring, diesel fuel and emission systems, assembly overhaul techniques and heavy vehicle safety procedures should be built up.
Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers

Drive heavy and tractor-trailer vehicles to complete freight tasks: check the vehicle and cargo securing before departure, transport according to route and time limits, record and handle anomalies en route, and complete handover and documents as required on arrival.

The focus of responsibility differs: drivers are responsible for transport safety and on-route handling, and daily checks and fault identification are part of their duties, but dismantling, assembly overhauls and emission-related repairs are not within a driver's scope of work; this occupation is responsible for repair quality and the reassembly of safety components but does not take on transport tasks or driving responsibility en route.

If you prefer driving and the pace of transport, you can choose the driver direction and obtain the corresponding driving qualification as required; if you prefer fault analysis and hands-on repair, this occupation is closer. The two work closely together in a fleet, and understanding each other's work helps in judging whether a vehicle can be repaired and whether it needs to be taken out of service.
Industrial machinery mechanics

The objects and basis differ: industrial machinery mechanics maintain factory production equipment and lines, arranging preventive maintenance and breakdown repair according to equipment maintenance procedures and the production rhythm; this occupation follows the manufacturer's vehicle service technical information and road transport and vehicle safety requirements, and its objects are vehicles powered by diesel engines and diesel engines, involving vehicle-specific steps such as lifting and road testing.

If you are interested in the general principles of mechanical structure, transmission and hydraulics and want fewer vehicle emission and road test steps, you can consider the industrial machinery maintenance direction; if you want to go deeper in vehicles and engines specifically, this occupation is more suitable. The two share basic knowledge of hydraulics, bearings and gears.
Millwrights (equipment installation and maintenance mechanics)

The focus of work differs: millwrights focus on equipment installation, alignment, truing and dismantling and moving, and the precision requirement shows in installation and alignment rather than fault diagnosis; this occupation has fault diagnosis, dismantling and assembly and overhaul as its daily core, with the reassembly of safety components and road test verification being its key steps.

If you prefer installation and alignment precision and the on-site layout of complete equipment sets, you can look at the millwright direction; if you would rather face vehicle faults and repair judgments every day, this occupation is more suitable. The common foundation is the use of measuring tools, tightening torque specifications and safe working habits.
Rail car repairers

The operating systems differ: rail car repairers work according to railway maintenance procedures and graded repair schedules, constrained by train operation organization and track work safety, and their pace is determined by the train timetable and maintenance windows; this occupation deals with road vehicles and diesel engines, its work is driven by the work order schedule and the customer's need for the vehicle, and road test verification is possible.

If you want to enter the rail transit industry and develop within a repair schedule system, you can consider the rail car maintenance direction; if you prefer diesel engine and assembly repair on road transport vehicles, this occupation is closer. Knowledge of brake systems and bearing fits is transferable between the two.
Tire repairers and changers

The scope of work differs: tire repairers and changers are responsible for special tasks such as mounting and demounting tires, patching and replacement, dynamic balancing and four-wheel alignment inspection and adjustment, and their scope is relatively focused; this occupation treats tire and wheel work as one link, with the main body being the diagnosis and overhaul of assemblies such as the engine, fuel and emissions, transmission, and brakes and steering.

If you want to get started quickly and focus on tire and wheel special tasks, you can start in the tire repair direction; if you want to build broader assembly diagnosis and overhaul capability, this occupation has more depth. Manual mounting and demounting and safe lifting are the shared foundation of both.

The relationship of AI and automation to this occupation needs to be viewed in three layers: first, technical capability — what diagnostic software, telematics and fault prediction tools can do; second, actual adoption — how much repair businesses and fleets really use them under cost, liability and compliance constraints; third, position outcomes — after adoption, is it a change in task structure, a change in skill requirements, or a change in the number of positions. Mixing the three layers together produces the two inaccurate claims that the job is bound to be replaced or that there is no impact at all.

The BLS description notes that many repair settings use computer diagnostics, which is not a measured test of generative AI adoption. The object of a fit judgment is the work itself, not a personality label. Every day this occupation involves troubleshooting faults item by item against the manual and measured values, hands-on dismantling and assembly in oily and noisy environments, responsibility for reassembling safety components, and writing the process into records that others can review. First consider whether you are willing to do these tasks and can accept such conditions, and then see whether the personality description fits.

First group of signals: whether you can stay patient when information is incomplete — fault symptoms are often vague and the customer's description may not match the measured data, requiring items to be ruled out one by one among several possibilities rather than replacing an assembly on first instinct.

Second group of signals: acceptance of manual and physical work — lifting heavy components, tightening high-torque bolts and working in confined spaces are routine; fine operation with the arms and fingers is also required, for example dismantling small parts and connecting fasteners.

Third group of signals: attitude to specifications and records — torque specifications, clearance tolerances, protective equipment and work order records are hard requirements, and omitting any one of them may affect safety or the determination of liability.

Fourth group of signals: judgement about safety and responsibility — for safety components such as brakes, steering and wheel bearings and for emission-related work, it is better to recheck one extra time than to rush; be willing to stop and ask when a task exceeds your capability.

Fifth group of signals: the way you learn — the technology of this occupation comes from manuals, fault codes and dismantling findings, and continuous learning of new models, new fuel and exhaust systems and electrical and alternative fuel systems is needed; one training course is not enough to remain competent over the long term.

Sixth group of signals: collaboration and communication — you need to communicate with service advisers, parts suppliers, team leaders and customers about faults, costs and delivery time, and accept quality inspectors' review of safety components.

Risk one: improper handling of safety components. Brakes, steering and wheel bearings are directly related to driving safety; if replacement parts do not meet specifications, if torques and clearances are not reassembled to specification, or if rechecks are omitted, this may lead to serious consequences such as brake failure or a wheel coming off. The control is to work strictly to manual specifications, use genuine and traceable parts, and remeasure and verify by road test after reassembly.

Risk two: personal risk in lifting, high-pressure and electrical work. Unstable support when lifting vehicles and assemblies, failure to depressurise a high-pressure fuel system, and missing protection for welding and live electrical work can all cause personal injury. The control is to use qualified supports and lifting gear, depressurise and isolate power according to procedure, wear protective equipment, and set up supervision for work in confined spaces.

Risk three: compliance risk in emission-related work. Temporarily replacing emission control devices or disabling the onboard emission diagnostic system to get a vehicle through an emission inspection is expressly prohibited work; if it happens, both the repair operator and the worker may bear responsibility. The control is to repair to standards and the manufacturer's technical requirements and to record test data truthfully.

Risk four: income and reputational risk arising from parts and labour time disputes. Using counterfeit or substandard parts, not itemising labour time and material fees, or providing an incomplete settlement statement all lead to rework and complaints; self-employed and piece-rate workers may also face customer arrears and business fluctuation. The control is to keep vouchers for the source of parts, issue settlement statements according to labour time allowances and charge standards, and avoid taking on work beyond your capability after promising a low price.

Risk five: skills becoming obsolete and career development stalling. The fuel, emission and electrical systems of diesel vehicles keep being updated, and alternative fuel and hybrid systems are expanding; if you only do repetitive part replacement over the long term without building up diagnostic and electrical capability, income and job choices will be limited. The control is to keep attending manufacturer and industry training, record the complex diagnostic cases you have handled, and gradually establish a specialism.

If you receive review opinions from quality inspectors or team leaders, treat them as a normal part of safety and quality rather than a denial of your personal ability; for opinions involving safety components, remeasure to specification before delivery.

paragraphs: First point on training, qualification and delivery boundaries: the education, major, experience and relaxation conditions in a recruitment notice must be read item by item; the fact that one item can be relaxed does not mean the other conditions can be substituted, nor does completing training mean being able to work independently.

Second point: the paper exercises and seven-day experience on this page are for career exploration only and do not constitute passing training, repair authorization, payment, outage or safe work permission; any real vehicle lifting, dismantling and assembly, electrical, welding, high-pressure fuel and emission-related work must be carried out according to procedure by personnel with the corresponding capability and authorization.

Third point: different qualifications prove different things — a vocational college course proves learning experience, industry certification proves capability in a specific direction, a commercial driving licence proves driving qualification, an occupational skill level certificate in mainland China describes skill level, and motor vehicle repair business filing constrains the operator rather than individual qualification; they cannot substitute for one another.

Fourth point: entering this occupation is not just enrolling on a course; first verify the target region's position definition, entry education, on-the-job training, certification and licence requirements, and the employer's specific requirements for safety and records, and then decide on the training investment.

The entry path on this page is based on verifiable preparation levels and entry requirements and is divided into three stages: first build safe work and basic servicing capability, then move into diagnosis and assembly repair, and finally develop a specialism or mentoring and team management capability. Each stage uses delivering a verifiable result under supervision as the basis for advancement, rather than automatic advancement by years of service.

The typical BLS entry in the United States is high school or equivalent, no related work experience, and long-term on-the-job training; employers may prefer a postsecondary diesel repair course, certification may be required or preferred, and a CDL may be needed for road tests of large bus or truck vehicles. The O*NET JobZone3/SVP6 to below 7 and the group-level 1—2 years of training do not guarantee that duration for every person in this occupation; the education responses of 39% postsecondary certificate and 37% high school are not law or the education composition of employees.

Motor vehicle repair operators in China file with the county-level transport authority of their location after registration, filing is free of charge, and the scope and category follow the business items. Article 12 requires at least 1 person each for the technical lead, quality inspection and reception and for each type of repair personnel in categories one and two; category three comprehensive minor repairs, engine, body, electrical and automatic transmission repair also require a technical lead and quality inspection, and this cannot be omitted. Quality inspection personnel must hold a compatible driving licence, so the driving threshold is not uniform for all repair workers; enterprise filing does not replace individual skills or position authority. The 2018 automotive repairer standard sets levels five to one and general education of junior high school; level five requires 1 accumulated year in this occupation or a specified related occupation or completion of an apprenticeship, and level four has different branches such as 4 years after the level five certificate, 6 accumulated years, or a qualification from a specified school major, with theory and skills and the applicable comprehensive review each passing at 60, and technicians and senior technicians undergoing a comprehensive review. The 2024 official annex adds the commercial vehicle repair worker job type under 4-12-01-01; the old standard's registration branches are not passed off as the current assessment notice for the new job type, and fees, actual duration and subsidies were not verified in this round.

items.title: Starter case material: a troubleshooting record for a fictional diesel truck

values: Day one: read and understand a service manual excerpt
Find publicly available diesel engine repair material and write out the torque or clearance specifications and inspection steps given by the manual
Day two: organise one set of measurement data
Using the three given sets of fictional measured values, judge which item is out of specification and write down the items that need remeasuring
Day three: write a troubleshooting checklist
List the causes to be ruled out and the corresponding inspection methods in the manual's order, marking the safety steps that cannot be omitted
Day four: write a work order record
State the cause of the fault, the handling method, replaced parts and items to be observed clearly, in no more than 300 characters
Day five: learn about the working conditions
Look at publicly available material on workshop work and protection requirements and write down whether you can accept working with oil, noise and confined spaces
Day six: compare adjacent directions
Choose two directions in the adjacent occupation comparison table on this page and write one sentence each on the difference in objects and responsibility
Day seven: verify the training and qualification paths
Find out separately the entry education, on-the-job training, certification and licence requirements of the target region, and write down what information is still missing

entries: Day seven judgement 1: whether you are willing to troubleshoot item by item against the manual and measured values rather than replacing parts by feel.
Day seven judgement 2: whether you accept working conditions with oil, dust, noise and confined spaces and are willing to wear protective equipment over the long term.
Day seven judgement 3: whether you are willing to sign for the reassembly of safety components and for records, and would rather recheck one extra time.
Day seven judgement 4: whether you are willing to keep learning new models, fuel and exhaust systems and electrical and alternative fuel systems.

Day seven judgement 5: whether you understand that completing training does not mean authorization to work independently, and that industry certification and a driving licence cannot substitute for one another.
Day seven judgement 6: whether you have found out the entry education, training and qualification requirements of the target region or country, rather than enrolling directly on a course.

Day seven judgement 7: if the answer to most of the above is yes, you can enter a supervised practical training or apprenticeship path; if most are no, it is better to learn about adjacent directions before deciding.

Preparation stage

Complete high school or equivalent education, take a vocational college or postsecondary diesel engine repair course, and master the use of measuring tools, the concepts of torque and clearance, and safe working requirements.
Working under supervision

Under the guidance of the mentor or team leader, complete basic servicing and dismantling and assembly tasks, check specifications against the manual, record on the work order, and accept review by quality inspectors.
Independently taking on routine repair
Be able to independently diagnose and repair common faults, replace and reassemble and recheck safety components, and write the process into a reviewable record.
Specialisation and mentoring

Develop a specialism in diagnosis, fuel injection and electrical work, assembly overhaul or fleet supervision, or take on mentoring and quality review duties; the scope of responsibility is still governed by the position and authorization.

entries.answer: A typical day unfolds by work order: after receiving the vehicle, confirm the fault symptoms and operating conditions with the customer or service adviser, read fault codes and instrument values, use test instruments, listening and road testing to rule items out and measure pressure, temperature, clearance and voltage; after confirming the cause, dismantle and inspect, replace or repair, reassemble to the manufacturer's specification and recheck torques and clearances, service the fuel injection and emission control devices, carry out routine servicing such as oil changes and lubrication, and finally verify by road test and complete the work order and replaced parts records. The work is mainly in the workshop, with occasional repairs at the roadside or at a work site.
entries.question: What is the specific daily work?

entries.answer: This occupation is a position that carries out repair work: responsible for diagnosis, dismantling, repair and overhaul, and for repair quality and the reassembly of safety components. Team leaders and workshop supervisors are responsible for work order allocation, progress and staff arrangements; the technical lead and quality inspection personnel are responsible for technical control and reviewing inspection conclusions (category one and two motor vehicle repair businesses in mainland China must have these two types of personnel). Workers must not replace the review of quality inspection personnel and do not bear operating or management responsibility.
entries.question: What is the difference from a supervisor or lead?

entries.answer: What the available public evidence supports is a change in the entry point of diagnosis and higher record requirements, not replacement. The relevant technology entries recorded by O*NET centre on diagnosis, testing and information query steps; the ILO occupational exposure study classifies this type of occupation as having limited exposure; the tasks of this occupation are mainly physical dismantling and assembly, measurement and on-site judgment, and dismantling conclusions and the reassembly of safety components must still be done by people. The BLS Occupational Outlook gives a 2025—2035 projection of +4%.
entries.question: How will AI affect or replace this occupation?

entries.answer: The clearest are diagnostic and testing steps such as reading fault codes, parameter trend analysis and similar case retrieval, and reminders for servicing scheduling; the O*NET task list has corresponding descriptions, but its technology entries only state technical availability, not the actual adoption proportion of enterprises. No verifiable substitution evidence has appeared for dismantling and overhaul, the reassembly of safety components, or human confirmation of emission-related work.
entries.question: Which tasks already have evidence of AI change?

entries.answer: Following the approach of the NIST AI risk management framework, three things should be verified: first, whether, after a tool gives a cause ranking, the cause can be verified or ruled out with the measurements and dismantling specified in the manual; second, whether physical clues such as abnormal noise, vibration and leakage can be recognised in confined and noisy environments; third, whether the diagnostic process, measured values and items to be observed can be completely recorded and accept review. All three can be tested in supervised actual work.
entries.question: Facing AI, which capabilities should still be prioritised for verification?

Do not dismantle real vehicles or carry out electrical, welding and high-pressure fuel system work unsupervised and without protection.

entries.answer: Four points should also be considered: first, working conditions — exposure to contaminants 85% every day, noise 81% every day, indoors but without environmental control 74% every day, requiring protective equipment to be worn over the long term; second, pace — a typical workweek over 40 hours accounts for 53%, and fleet positions involve shifts and breakdown repair; third, the direction of technical change — the share of emission and electrical related work is rising and continuous learning is needed; fourth, regional differences — demand is more concentrated where fleets and freight hubs are located. These factors affect long-term fit no less than the wage level.

The 2018 automotive repairer standard sets levels five to one and general education of junior high school; level five requires 1 accumulated year in this occupation or a specified related occupation or completion of an apprenticeship, and level four has different branches such as 4 years after the level five certificate, 6 accumulated years, or a qualification from a specified school major, with theory and skills and the applicable comprehensive review each passing at 60, and technicians and senior technicians undergoing a comprehensive review. Motor vehicle repair operators in China file with the county-level transport authority of their location after registration, filing is free of charge, and the scope and category follow the business items. Article 12 requires at least 1 person each for the technical lead, quality inspection and reception and for each type of repair personnel in categories one and two; category three comprehensive minor repairs, engine, body, electrical and automatic transmission repair also require a technical lead and quality inspection, and this cannot be omitted. description.text: Diesel service technicians and mechanics (O*NET-SOC 49-3031.00) inspect, diagnose, repair and overhaul buses, trucks and other vehicles powered by diesel engines, and maintain and repair various diesel engines: dismantling and assembling with hand and power tools, checking safety components such as brakes and steering, reading codes with instruments and diagnostic tools, confirming faults by listening and road testing, dismantling and overhauling engines and assemblies, servicing fuel injection and emission control devices, carrying out routine servicing and recording and handing over. United States scope: in the 2025 wage data the median annual wage is 61,770 USD (median hourly 29.70 USD), with annual percentiles of 44,530 / 50,540 / 61,770 / 75,470 / 88,740 USD; 2024 employment is about 319,900 people, growth of 1% to 2% over 2024—2034 with about 26,500 projected openings (the BLS Occupational Outlook separately gives 316,000 positions in 2025, +4% for 2025—2035 and about 24,400 annual average openings); the interest code is RCI. Mainland China: motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing management, practitioners must follow safe production operating procedures, and the occupational path corresponds to the automotive repairer (including commercial vehicle repair worker) occupational skill level; public statistics have not established an occupational-level wage scope for this occupation, and this page marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.summary: Diesel service technicians and mechanics (United States side O*NET-SOC 49-3031.00; titled Diesel Service Technicians and Mechanics by the BLS Occupational Outlook) are personnel who inspect, diagnose, repair and overhaul buses, trucks and other vehicles powered by diesel engines, and maintain and repair various diesel engines, including mechanics who mainly work on automotive or marine diesel engines: using hand tools such as screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, pressure gauges and precision instruments, and power tools such as pneumatic wrenches, lathes, welding equipment, jacks and lifting gear; checking safety components such as the brake system, steering mechanism and wheel bearings, lifting vehicles and heavy components with hydraulic jacks or lifting gear, adjusting and replacing brake linings, aligning wheels, tightening to the specified torque and reassembling; connecting test instruments to equipment to read gauges and meters in order to diagnose faults, reading codes with diagnostic tools, confirming problems by listening and road testing, dismantling and overhauling internal combustion engines, pumps, generators, transmissions, clutches and differentials, repairing or replacing pistons, bearings, gears and valves, servicing fuel injection systems and emission control devices, carrying out routine servicing such as oil changes, battery checks and lubrication, and disposing of waste oil and reducing solid waste as required by environmental operating rules. United States scope: in the 2025 wage data for this occupation the median annual wage is 61,770 USD (median hourly 29.70 USD), with annual percentiles of 44,530 / 50,540 / 61,770 / 75,470 / 88,740 USD (hourly percentiles 21.41 / 24.30 / 29.70 / 36.29 / 42.66); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 319,900 people, growth of 1% to 2% over 2024—2034 (below average) and about 26,500 projected openings, while the BLS Occupational Outlook gives another scope of 316,000 positions in 2025, +4% for 2025—2035 (about average), a net increase of 11,400 and about 24,400 annual average openings; the preparation level is Job Zone Three (medium preparation, SVP 6.0 to below 7.0), usually requiring 1—2 years of training, with apprenticeship opportunities; the interest code is RCI; the work context includes exposure to contaminants 85% every day, using hands to handle or feel objects and tools 80% continuously, wearing common protective or safety equipment 78% every day, face-to-face discussion with individuals and teams 90% every day, and being in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 68% every day. Mainland China scope: diesel vehicle repair is a motor vehicle repair business and automotive repairer activity; the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair apply filing management to repair operations and require repair businesses to have the corresponding technical personnel, with practitioners following safe production operating procedures; the national occupational skill standard for automotive repairers sets levels from level five/junior worker to level one/senior technician, and in July 2024 the commercial vehicle repair worker job type was further added under the automotive repairer occupation; public statistics have not published occupational-level wages corresponding to this occupation, and this page retains the gap as it stands.
